messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: perf-cliff detected in kv-cache + batch-scheduler hybrid traffic pattern. Severity: P2. Notifying oncall.

maria (oncall): @here seeing tail latencies spike to ~2.8s for user-facing gen requests. Multiple customers reporting timeouts. Any initial hypotheses? :eyes: 

jordan (sre): I see simultaneous increase in paging events and continuous-batching queue lengths on region-us-west-2. KV cache working set doubled in 5m. Logging snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15T02:41:23Z] kv_cache.evictions/sec=1204 active_pages=18234 paging_ops=893
[2026-03-15T02:41:24Z] batch_scheduler.pending_short=240 pending_long=18 avg_batch_ms=48
[2026-03-15T02:41:25Z] kv_cache.kv_hits=0.62 kv_miss_cost_ms=220
```

alex (eng-runtime): This looks like mixing long context completions with lots of short chat/LLM requests. Continuous batching is aggregating mixed lengths and overflowing the KV prefetch window which trips paging and heavy disk I/O. I can reproduce locally with mixed workload.

maria (oncall): Is there a safe quick mitigation we can flip? Reduce batch assembly timeout or limit long request packing?

lee (eng-platform): We can push an emergency config change to the scheduler: set `batch_timeout_ms` -> 20 and enable `prefer_short_request_pack=true` in the runtime. That should reduce short-request tail latency but might penalize throughput for long jobs.

alex (eng-runtime): Agreed. Also toggle `kv_prefetch.enabled=false` for affected node pool to reduce aggressive prefetching while we investigate. That should lower paging.

jordan (sre): I approve the config flips for a temporary 30-min window. Who can roll?

maria (oncall): @deploy-bot can you run the rollout? Patch id: rollout-9876. Command: 
```
deploy-bot apply-config --env=prod --pool=us-west-2 --changes 'batch_timeout_ms=20,prefer_short_request_pack=true,kv_prefetch.enabled=false' --tag=incident-2112345678
```

deploy-bot: Accepted. Starting canary rollout to 5% nodes in us-west-2. Will report health.

(2m later)
deploy-bot: Canary update succeeded on 5% nodes. Observability: tail_p95 latency decreased from 2.8s -> 0.9s for short requests. Paging ops reduced ~70%.

raj (customer-success): We have an affected customer (acct: summit-analytics) on us-west-2 who reported 504s starting ~02:37. They are requesting ETA. 

maria (oncall): Tell them we're mitigating and turned on a temporary scheduler + kv_prefetch rollback. ETA 15-30m. I'll take ownership of the customer comms. @raj please send the note and loop back.

alex (eng-runtime): Observed side-effect: long-running requests p95 increased by ~400ms in the canary due to fewer co-packings. Acceptable for short-term. We'll watch throughput.

jordan (sre): Running a quick diagnostic to ensure no spillover into other regions. So far only us-west-2 showed the paging spike.

lee (eng-platform): Logging additional metrics to incident dashboard. Added `batch_mix_ratio` and `kv_prefetch_queue_depth` graphs.

(8m later)
deploy-bot: Canary health stable at 5%. Promoting to 50% nodes.

maria (oncall): After promotion, customer reports cleared and global short-tail p95 back near baseline. Any permanent fix proposals?

alex (eng-runtime): Root cause: continuous batching allowed long requests to anchor batches, artificially increasing batch assembly time and triggering aggressive kv prefetches which expanded memory/paging footprint. Short-term we limited mixing and prefetch. Longer-term: two tracks: 1) batch_scheduler: add explicit queue separation for short/long workloads + enforcement of max_pack_time per job class; 2) kv runtime: adaptive prefetch with per-tenant heuristics and backpressure to avoid blowups.

jordan (sre): I'll open an incident ticket and schedule a postmortem. Need to quantify customer impact window (02:37-02:52) and number of affected requests.

raj (customer-success): Sent template update to Summit Analytics. They acknowledged and appreciate quick response.

maria (oncall): Handing off to eng-runtime and platform for next steps. Oncall remains available for 2hr follow-up.

alex (eng-runtime): Creating a PR for the scheduler change and a short-term patch to disallow mixing of >80 token and <80 token requests in the same batch. Reference: PR #4921.

lee (eng-platform): We'll schedule a canary rollout for the PR tomorrow with a targeted experiment. Also adding an alert for `kv_prefetch.queue_depth > 1000` to trigger early mitigation.

(End of thread)
